modelNote:
Create a clean, professional portrait infographic for university students summarising the research paper: “Decreasing students’ stress through time management training: an intervention study” by Alexander Häfner, Armin Stock & Verena Oberst, Eur J Psychol Educ (2015) 30:81–94, DOI 10.1007/s10212-014-0229-2, published online 6 September 2014.

Strict content rules: use only the text and numbers below; no outside facts; do not calculate new numbers; keep exact wording for strength of claims; spell all words correctly; perceived stress must be labelled “Stress (tension)”; “demands” means perceived, self-reported demands. Use fewer, larger text blocks, icons, simple charts/diagrams. Tall portrait layout, clear hierarchy.

Infographic structure:

TOP TITLE:
“Can time management training reduce student stress?”
Subtitle: “Häfner, Stock & Oberst (2015) | Undergraduate intervention study”

SECTION 1 — Purpose (icon: question mark + clock)
Text: “Research question: Is it possible to increase perceived control of time and reduce Stress (tension) through time management training in a student sample?”
Small hypothesis chips:
“Control of time ↑”
“Stress (tension) ↓”
“Demands unchanged”

SECTION 2 — Sample & design (icon: students + calendar)
Use concise callout cards:
“48 local undergraduate students began”
“23 completed all questionnaires”
“Mean age = 23.30 years (SD = 2.80)”
“About half female: 52%”
“Medium-sized German university”
Design timeline: 
“Time 1: directly before training” → “4 h time management training” → “Time 2: 2 weeks after” → “Time 3: 4 weeks after”
Design label: “Non-equivalent dependent variable design”
Control variable note: “Demands were measured as a variable expected not to change.”

SECTION 3 — What the training involved (icon: checklist/target/calendar)
Title: “4-hour training content”
Five numbered blocks:
“1 Prioritizing”
“2 Concrete, proximal and challenging goals”
“3 Strategy development + possible obstacles”
“4 Daily planning”
“5 Monitoring task completion”
Small note: “Participants reflected on academic tasks and extracurricular activities.”

SECTION 4 — Key measures (icon: sliders)
Three pill labels with exact naming:
“Perceived control of time: 10 items, 1–5”
“Stress (tension): 5 items, 1–5”
“Demands: 5 items, 1–5”
Small note: “Time management behaviour: 18 items, 1–5”

SECTION 5 — Main findings with simple line chart (largest visual area)
Create a clear line chart with x-axis: “Before”, “2 weeks”, “4 weeks”; y-axis not necessarily scaled, but show exact values next to points. Use three coloured lines:
Line A green: “Perceived control of time” values 2.75, 2.89, 3.05. Annotate: “2 weeks: tendency in expected direction, p = 0.08”; “4 weeks: significant, F(1, 22) = 11.62, partial η² = 0.35, p < 0.01”.
Line B red/orange: “Stress (tension)” values 3.30, 2.96, 3.03. Annotate: “2 weeks: significant, F(1, 22) = 8.22, partial η² = 0.27, p < 0.01”; “4 weeks: significant, F(1, 22) = 5.75, partial η² = 0.21, p = 0.03”.
Line C grey: “Demands” values 3.59, 3.35, 3.46. Annotate: “No significant changes: 2 weeks t(22) = 1.68, p = 0.107; 4 weeks t(22) = 1.19, p = 0.251”.
Legend must identify all three lines.

SECTION 6 — Transfer of training strategies (icon: arrow + checklist)
Title: “Did students use the strategies?”
Show mini upward arrow chart for “Time management behaviour” values: 3.01 → 3.19 → 3.31.
Text: “Significant increase from before training to 4 weeks after: t(22) = 2.67, p < 0.01, ε′ = 0.79.”
Text: “Nearly significant increase from before training to 2 weeks after: t(22) = 1.62, p = 0.060, ε′ = 0.48.”
Text: “Authors: trainees transferred the training content to daily work at least to some extent.”

SECTION 7 — Who seemed to benefit more? (icon: two student groups)
Text: “Students with no or little prior experience seemed to profit more than students with moderate or some experience, especially with respect to Stress (tension).”
Two small comparison cards:
“No/little experience: n = 14”
“Moderate/some experience: n = 9”
Optional exact effect-size note: “At 4 weeks, ε′ = 0.78 for perceived control of time and ε′ = 0.64 for Stress (tension) in the no/little group; ε′ = 0.34 and ε′ = 0.13 in the moderate/some group.”

SECTION 8 — Main limitation & takeaway (bottom, high contrast box)
Limitation title: “Main limitation”
Text: “Small sample size; the authors describe the study as preliminary and call for larger samples. They also note that a control group or pseudo-training group would be a methodological improvement.”
Takeaway title: “Takeaway”
Text: “In this preliminary study, a 4-hour time management training was followed by lower Stress (tension), higher perceived control of time after 4 weeks, and no significant change in demands. The authors conclude that time management training might be beneficial for undergraduate students’ well-being.”

Visual style: modern academic infographic, portrait A4 ratio, white background, dark navy text, accents in teal, green, orange/red, and grey. Use simple icons, ample whitespace, readable typography, no tiny dense text. Ensure all words and statistical notation are legible and spelled correctly. Avoid any claim that the study proves effects; use “authors conclude”, “might”, “preliminary”, “reported”.
